summary.headline: Atlanta Electricals Q2 FY27 revenue rose 23.1% YoY to INR390.1 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 15.3% on firm-price contracts and ~INR180 crore of deferred deliveries.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew 23.1% YoY to INR390.1 crore, while gross margin fell to 26.6% from 30.9% and EBITDA margin to 15.3% from 17.3%. Management attributed the squeeze to elevated transformer oil, copper and steel prices on firm-price orders (about 15% of quarterly revenue) and Gujarat monsoon disruptions that delayed customer acceptance of finished transformers worth about INR180 crore. PAT rose 28% YoY to INR32.1 crore, helped by lower finance costs. Order book reached INR3,197 crore, up 54.5% YoY, but Q2 order inflow was only about INR421 crore as management chose to limit 220 kV and below bookings.

segments.name: Transformers - 220 kV and below (current book)
segments.commentary: About 47% of the order book is 220 kV class per management. Management said it deliberately limited new 220 kV and below bookings in Q2 given a large Q1 booking base.

segments.name: Transformers - 400 kV class
segments.commentary: About 8.6% of the order book is 400 kV class (INR184 crore per management). First 315 MVA, 400 kV unit commenced manufacturing on 26 Oct 2026; commercial contribution targeted in Q4 FY27 after testing.

segments.name: Export / US
segments.commentary: First US order for a special duty transformer, for a new US transformer plant. US inquiries of about 120 transformers (9,300 MVA). Medium-term aspiration of exports at about 15% of revenue within 2 years.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin for FY27 and FY28 expected in the 16% to 18% range; management said it remains firm on achieving this in both years.
3-year revenue growth aspiration of approximately 40% CAGR reiterated; CEO-level comment that 40% is a minimum, and management said FY28 is covered but would not give FY29 guidance.
About 70% of the INR180 crore deferred orders already dispatched in October; remainder expected in Q3 FY27, subject to customer site readiness.
Remaining firm-price orders (about 10-12% of order book per CFO, 3-4% per COO) expected to be substantially executed in Q3 FY27, with price revisions reportedly obtained from customers.
Management expects H2 to be stronger than H1 seasonally and expects margin correction in Q3 and Q4; target utilisation of 80%.
capex_capacity: Dedicated inverter duty transformer (IDT) plant: about 5,000 MVA capacity, capex INR65 crore, civil work complete, commissioning expected before end-Q3 FY27; 33 kV IDT production moves from Unit 2 to free Unit 2 for 66 and 132 kV classes.

Tank and radiator backward integration via AE Components: capex about INR193 crore (INR196 crore cited later in Q&A, likely the same project), groundbreaking done, commissioning targeted October 2027. Funded mainly through internal accruals, with term loans tied up but undrawn as a backup.
Utilisation as stated in Q&A: Unit 1 at 60%, Unit 2 at 40%, Bangalore at about 90%, Vadod at about 30%, Jambusar (765 kV plant) at about 7-8%.

765 kV: in-house design of first 765 kV reactor started; production targeted in Q4 FY27 with completion and testing between Q4 FY27 and Q1 FY28. International technology partnership not progressed due to sanctions constraints; management says partnership remains open.
Vadod facility has approvals from NTPC Solar, NTPC Renewables, Tata Power, KPTCL and Punjab Transmission Company.
demand_pricing: Order book INR3,196.97 crore at 30 Sep 2026, vs INR3,116.63 crore at end-June and about INR2,069 crore a year ago (+54.5% YoY).
Q2 order inflow about INR421 crore; management called the slowdown a deliberate decision to limit 220 kV and below orders, and cited commodity volatility delaying some L1 tenders.
Inquiry pipeline about INR19,464 crore. Battery energy storage pipeline of about 3,400 MVA worth INR184 crore.

Pricing: majority of orders carry price variation clauses. Since the Middle East conflict began in March 2026, new quotes are mostly on price-variation basis; management said no pressure yet seen on pricing or inquiry pipeline.
LOI worth INR193.92 crore from APTRANSCO for 12 units of 160 MVA, 220 kV class autotransformers. 12 new customers added in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 765 kV plant ramp-up delayed by the lack of a technology partner, and will the designs align with Power Grid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the partner route remains open but it is proceeding in-house; 765 kV is in Unit 5 and 400 kV in Unit 4 in parallel. COO said CEA has standardised 400 and 765 kV specifications, so designs are acceptable to Power Grid and other Indian customers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did order inflow fall about 55% QoQ, and what to expect in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO-level answer: a management decision to cautiously book 220 kV and below orders after a large Q1 booking base covering about 1.5 years; 400 kV and above will be the focus once a 400 kV prototype is ready. Management said the INR3,000 crore-plus book covers visibility.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the order book is firm-price, and will new orders carry price variation clauses?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said firm-price share is 10-12%; COO later said 3-4%. COO said new quotes since March are price-variation based, with at most 1-2% of the last six months' book on firm price.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR193 crore capex be funded, and is more capex planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Funded mainly from internal accruals, with bank term loans tied up but not drawn. No other major capex planned beyond small staff housing projects.

qa_highlights.question: Will the remaining firm-price orders keep margins down in Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: COO said customers agreed to price revisions bringing 2025 booking prices in line with current levels, so no major negative margin impact is expected in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA margins reach the earlier 18-19% aspiration, and what is the pricing outlook from new capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO reiterated the 16-18% FY27-FY28 range, with H2 expected to lift margins through operating leverage. COO said no pricing pressure seen so far, though some peers are expanding capacity.

risks_watch: Gross margin compression on remaining firm-price orders and commodity volatility (transformer oil, copper, steel) that management says is still a key factor to monitor.
Customer site readiness: about 30% of the INR180 crore deferred orders is still pending dispatch, with completion targeted in Q3 FY27.
Inventory rose to INR632.9 crore from INR364.1 crore in six months, creating working capital pressure. Management expects it to unwind as deferred orders are executed.
Supply chain risk for critical components (bushings, containers) due to typhoons and Middle East conflict; management says the issue is temporary.
Execution risk on 400 kV first unit (commercial contribution Q4 FY27) and 765 kV production (Q4 FY27), with the technology partner route stalled by sanctions.
Order inflow slowdown in Q2 and the low utilisation of Vadod (30%) and Jambusar (7-8%) plants; the IDT and backward integration commissioning dates are key checkpoints.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term outlook and margin range, but defensive about the Q2 miss, attributing it to weather, commodity costs and deferred deliveries. Management was evasive on FY29 targets and US margin uplift, and gave inconsistent answers on firm-price order share (10-12% vs 3-4%).
key_quotes: Importantly, these represent deferred deliveries and not cancellations and these orders continue to remain part of our order book.
We maintain that our EBITDA margin for FY27 and FY28 would be ranging around 16% to 18%, and we are still firm on the belief that we will be achieving this margin in current year and coming year.
Green Energy Corridors will definitely improve the demand, but, on our side, we will still try and at least commit 40%.

growth.why: Management reiterates ~40% revenue CAGR (called a minimum) for FY27-FY28 and 16-18% EBITDA margin, backed by a INR3,197 crore order book (+54.5% YoY) and a 5,000 MVA IDT plant due before end-Q3 FY27, though Q2 inflow of ~INR421 crore was weak and the 40% target lacks a year-by-year bridge.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin fell to 15.3% from 17.3% in Q2, but management guides 16-18% for FY27-FY28 and expects margin correction in Q3 and Q4 as remaining firm-price orders (3-12% of book, sources conflict) are executed with price revisions obtained.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 5,000 MVA inverter duty transformer plant (capex INR65 crore, civil work complete) is due for commissioning before end-Q3 FY27, with 400 kV unit commercial contribution and 765 kV production targeted Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Order book of INR3,197 crore (+54.5% YoY) and ~INR180 crore deferred deliveries (70% dispatched in October) support volume growth, though Q2 order inflow of ~INR421 crore was weak and Bangalore is at ~90% utilisation vs Vadod at 30%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is mixed (Unit 1 60%, Unit 2 40%, Vadod 30%, Jambusar 7-8%, Bangalore ~90%) and management said no other major capex is planned beyond small staff housing, so a new announcement is possible but not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held the 16-18% EBITDA margin and ~40% revenue CAGR (called a minimum) without raising them, and Q2 margin fell to 15.3% with the H1 margin at 16%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Commodity volatility, customer site readiness (about 30% of INR180 crore still pending) and 400 kV/765 kV execution risk could push margins or timelines below the 16-18% range, though management is firm on it.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: First 315 MVA 400 kV unit commenced manufacturing 26 Oct 2026 with commercial contribution targeted Q4 FY27, and first 765 kV reactor production targeted Q4 FY27.

rows.label: 400 kV and above order focus
rows.why: Management is limiting 220 kV and below bookings (Q2 inflow ~INR421 crore, down ~55% QoQ) and says 400 kV and above will be the focus once the 400 kV prototype is ready; 400 kV is ~8.6% of book (INR184 crore).

rows.label: US special duty transformer and US plant
rows.why: First US order for a special duty transformer received, with ~120 transformers (9,300 MVA) in US inquiries and an aspiration of exports at ~15% of revenue within 2 years, but no US margin uplift was quantified.

rows.label: Inventory unwind as deferred orders dispatch
rows.why: Inventory rose to INR632.9 crore from INR364.1 crore (+74%) in six months; management expects it to unwind as ~30% of the INR180 crore deferred orders are executed in Q3 FY27.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 16-18% margin range, IDT commissioning and the ~40% CAGR minimum, but defensive on the Q2 margin miss and order slowdown, and inconsistent on firm-price share (10-12% CFO vs 3-4% COO); analysts pressed on order inflow and margin path.
